sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，一个专注于设计之美及其周围文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至在黑胶唱片时代我在夜总会当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带着300张你最珍贵的藏品去上班，你把DJ台变成了一个充满美丽50年历史艺术品的微型流动流行博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在可以在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》的我，迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, President Trump's new budget proposal would add trillions of dollars to the federal deficit and Republicans aren't talking about it.
sentences.zh: 今天，特朗普总统的新预算提案将为联邦赤字增加数万亿美元，而共和党人却对此闭口不谈。

sentences.en: Why, no one should be surprised.
sentences.zh: 为什么呢，没有人应该感到惊讶。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, February 14th.
sentences.zh: 今天是2月14日，星期三。

sentences.en: We're a country that has $19 trillion in debt.
sentences.zh: 我们是一个负债19万亿美元的国家。

sentences.en: We're in trouble.
sentences.zh: 我们陷入困境了。

sentences.en: As a candidate, Donald Trump was very critical of the size of the national debt.
sentences.zh: 作为候选人，唐纳德·特朗普对国债的规模提出了严厉批评。

sentences.en: Jim Tankersley covers taxes and the economy for The Times.
sentences.zh: 吉姆·坦克雷斯利为《时报》报道税收和经济。

sentences.en: But the fact is, we're at $19 trillion.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，我们的债务已经达到19万亿美元。

sentences.en: We owe $19 trillion.
sentences.zh: 我们欠了19万亿美元。

sentences.en: So we have $19 trillion in debt.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有19万亿美元的债务。

sentences.en: We have to get rid of it.
sentences.zh: 我们必须摆脱它。

sentences.en: We have to start at least knocking the heck out of it.
sentences.zh: 我们必须至少开始狠狠地削减它。

sentences.en: And very much cast it as sort of a symbol of the decline of America.
sentences.zh: 并且在很大程度上把它塑造成美国衰落的一种象征。

sentences.en: We just can't go on like this.
sentences.zh: 我们简直不能再这样下去了。

sentences.en: We've been mismanaged.
sentences.zh: 我们的管理出了问题。

sentences.en: We've been misrun.
sentences.zh: 我们的治理出了问题。

sentences.en: We don't know what the hell we're doing.
sentences.zh: 我们根本不知道自己在搞什么鬼。

sentences.en: By the way, when you owe $20 trillion, wouldn't it be really nice if you did have somebody that understood debt?
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，当你欠下20万亿美元时，如果你真的有一个懂债务的人，那岂不是太棒了吗？

sentences.en: And Donald Trump was going to be well-positioned to take care of it.
sentences.zh: 而唐纳德·特朗普将处于能够妥善处理此事的位置。

sentences.en: Boy, am I good at solving debt probleMs. Nobody can solve it like me.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我在解决债务问题上有多擅长。没有人能像我一样解决它。

sentences.en: One moment, he even promised in an interview with The Washington Post that he would pay it off entirely if he was president for eight years.
sentences.zh: 有一刻，他在接受《华盛顿邮报》采访时甚至承诺，如果他当总统八年，他将把债务全部还清。

sentences.en: And then what happens when Trump takes office?
sentences.zh: 然后当特朗普上台时会发生什么？

sentences.en: Donald Trump takes office and...
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普上台了，然后……

sentences.en: It doesn't sound like President Trump is remotely concerned about deficit spending.
sentences.zh: 听起来特朗普总统对赤字开支一点也不关心。

sentences.en: Surprise, surprise, the United States keeps adding to the debt.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，美国不断在增加债务。

sentences.en: In his first year in office, Donald Trump is going to increase the national debt.
sentences.zh: 在他执政的第一年，唐纳德·克朗普将增加国债。

sentences.en: He spends money, just like every president before him, and in this case, more than he is bringing in.
sentences.zh: 他花钱大手大脚，就像他之前的每一位总统一样，而这一次，花得比他收入的还要多。

sentences.en: And then the president pushes a tax bill through the Congress, which he signs in December.
sentences.zh: 然后总统将一项税收法案强行通过国会，并在12月将其签署成法。

sentences.en: Many economists are challenging this as a magic wand of growth, saying the cuts could increase the national debt by trillions.
sentences.zh: 许多经济学家对这种作为增长魔杖的做法提出质疑，称这些减税措施可能会使国债增加数万亿美元。

sentences.en: Which will add at least a trillion dollars to deficits, depending on which outside estimate you believe.
sentences.zh: 这至少会给赤字增加一万亿美元，具体取决于你相信哪家外部评估机构。

sentences.en: The president's 2019 budget was delivered to the House Budget Committee today.
sentences.zh: 总统的2019年预算案今天已递交给众议院预算委员会。

sentences.en: And beyond all that, after he's already done a lot in his first year to add to the debt, he proposes a budget which foresees next year a trillion dollar deficit almost,
sentences.zh: 除此之外，在他第一年为了增加债务已经做了很多事情之后，他提出了一项预算，预计明年的赤字将接近一万亿美元，

sentences.en: which is way higher than the end of the Obama years.
sentences.zh: 这比奥巴马执政末期要高得多。

sentences.en: In all, it would add a trillion dollars to the deficit.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，它将使赤字增加一万亿美元。

sentences.en: Seeking huge spending increases without even a pretense to balance the books.
sentences.zh: 在甚至连平衡账目的借口都没有的情况下，谋求巨额开支增长。

sentences.en: And an additional $7 trillion added to the debt over the next 10 years.
sentences.zh: 在未来10年里，债务还将额外增加7万亿美元。

sentences.en: And that is based on incredibly optimistic economic assumptions, which probably won't come true.
sentences.zh: 这是基于极其乐观的经济假设，这些假设可能不会成为现实。

sentences.en: Meaning that the debt could be even bigger.
sentences.zh: 这意味着债务甚至可能会变得更大。

sentences.en: Yeah, that means that it will probably get even more debt than he is forecasting.
sentences.zh: 是的，这意味着他的债务可能会比他预测的还要多。

sentences.en: And Jim, I have a sense of what these words we're using refer to.
sentences.zh: 吉姆，我大致明白我们使用的这些词指的是什么了。

sentences.en: The national debt and the deficit.
sentences.zh: 国债和赤字。

sentences.en: But what exactly do these two words mean?
sentences.zh: 但这两个词到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: And what are Trump's proposals doing to both of them?
sentences.zh: 特朗普的提案对这两者又有什么影响？

sentences.en: So the deficit is the difference between the amount of money that the government lays out every year and the amount of money it takes in for taxes.
sentences.zh: 因此，赤字就是政府每年支出的资金数额与通过税收收入获得的资金数额之间的差额。

sentences.en: And that deficit needs to be filled some way.
sentences.zh: 这个赤字需要以某种方式来填补。

sentences.en: You have to be able to pay your bills.
sentences.zh: 你必须有能力支付你的账单。

sentences.en: So the government borrows the money to pay that deficit.
sentences.zh: 所以政府借钱来弥补这个赤字。

sentences.en: And over time, the amount of money that the government has borrowed piles up.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，政府借款的金额越积越多。

sentences.en: And voila, that's the debt.
sentences.zh: 瞧，这就是债务。

sentences.en: So just to be clear, deficits lead to debt.
sentences.zh: 所以明确一点，赤字导致了债务。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: And there's really two ways you can bring down a deficit.
sentences.zh: 减少赤字实际上有两种方法。

sentences.en: One is you can raise taxes.
sentences.zh: 一种是你可以提高税收。

sentences.en: You can bring in more money, which will cover the cost of all your spending.
sentences.zh: 你可以获得更多的资金，这将涵盖你所有的开支成本。

sentences.en: The other is you can cut spending.
sentences.zh: 另一种是你可以削减开支。

sentences.en: The big things we spend money on are the military or social safety net programs like Medicare and Social Security.
sentences.zh: 我们花钱的大头是军事，或者像医疗保险和社会保障这样的社会安全网项目。

sentences.en: President Trump is actually spending more than President Obama was at the end of his second term.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统目前的支出实际上比奥巴马总统在他第二个任期结束时还要多。

sentences.en: And he's cut taxes.
sentences.zh: 而且他还减税了。

sentences.en: So he's not really doing either.
sentences.zh: 所以他其实两样都没做。

sentences.en: So to summarize this, this new president who had campaigned so outspokenly against both deficits and what deficits create, national debt, is making both of those bigger,
sentences.zh: 总而言之，这位曾经公开反对赤字以及赤字所产生的产物——国债的新总统，却正在把这两者搞得更大，

sentences.en: which feels surprising given that he is a Republican.
sentences.zh: 考虑到他是一名共和党人，这让人感觉有些意外。

sentences.en: It feels surprising, but it maybe shouldn't be given the history over the last couple of decades of Republican presidents.
sentences.zh: 这感觉很意外，但考虑到过去几十年里共和党总统的历史，或许它本不该让人意外。

sentences.en: The federal deficit is outrageous.
sentences.zh: 联邦赤字简直荒唐透顶。

sentences.en: For example, Ronald Reagan, 1980, takes office after having campaigned on a promise to balance the budget.
sentences.zh: 例如，罗纳德·里根在1980年带着平衡预算的竞选承诺上台。

sentences.en: And what does he do?
sentences.zh: 他做了什么？

sentences.en: This represents $750 billion in tax cuts over the next five years.
sentences.zh: 这代表着在未来五年内减税7500亿美元。

sentences.en: And this is only the beginning.
sentences.zh: 而这仅仅是个开始。

sentences.en: He cuts taxes.
sentences.zh: 他削减了税收。

sentences.en: And deficits start to go up.
sentences.zh: 赤字开始上升。

sentences.en: And then...
sentences.zh: 然后……

sentences.en: The surest way to make American products more competitive is to spur innovation, enterprise, and productivity by cutting tax rates again.
sentences.zh: 使美国产品更具竞争力的最确切方法，是通过再次降低税率来激发创新、企业活力和生产力。

sentences.en: And he spends more in the military.
sentences.zh: 他在军事上投入了更多资金。

sentences.en: And deficits go up further.
sentences.zh: 赤字进一步上升。

sentences.en: And you end up with not a big paragon of fiscal responsibility, but in fact, with much more debt than when he took office.
sentences.zh: 你最终得到的不是一个财政责任的楷模，事实上，其债务比他上台时要多得多。

sentences.en: Is there any political cost to Ronald Reagan for campaigning on a message of tackling deficits and actually making those deficits bigger?
sentences.zh: 罗纳德·里根以解决赤字为竞选口号，却实际把赤字搞得更大，这是否让他付出了任何政治代价？

sentences.en: There certainly was criticism of President Reagan for that,
sentences.zh: 里根总统为此当然遭到了批评，

sentences.en: but you have to remember the way Republicans in particular think about the Reagan experience was cutting taxes and delivering strong economic growth, which he did,
sentences.zh: 但你必须记住，共和党人看待里根经历的方式是减税并带来了强劲的经济增长——他也确实做到了，

sentences.en: and achieving a big military win, if you can call it that, over the Soviet Union at the end of the Cold War, sort of justified the borrowing in the eyes of the American public.
sentences.zh: 并在冷战结束时在苏联身上取得了巨大的军事胜利（如果可以这样称的话），在广大美国公众看来，这为借债行为提供了某种正当理由。

sentences.en: And he didn't really get criticized for it or pay as large of a political price as you would have expected, perhaps,
sentences.zh: 他并没有真正因此受到批评，也没有付出你可能预料到的那么大的政治代价，

sentences.en: given the degree to which it was central to his campaign for the White House in the first place.
sentences.zh: 鉴于这一主张原本是他竞选白宫的核心议题。

sentences.en: With the Democrats now in the control of the United States Congress, both houses, we're facing government by gridlock in Washington, with spending skyrocketing out of control.
sentences.zh: 随着民主党现在控制了美国国会的两院，我们在华盛顿面临着由于党派僵局导致的政府瘫痪，支出也失控般飙升。

sentences.en: So Ronald Reagan leaves office, still popular, and he is replaced by his vice president, George H.W.
sentences.zh: 因此，罗纳德·里根带着依旧很高的支持率卸任，接替他的是他的副总统乔治·H·W·布什。

sentences.en: Bush.
sentences.zh: 布什。

sentences.en: Good legislation thrown aside for pork barrel programs and a budget deficit looming over our children's children.
sentences.zh: 好的立法被抛在一边，取而代之的是照顾地方利益的项目，而预算赤字正笼罩在我们子孙后代的头上。

sentences.en: Who wins a fairly convincing victory and comes into office and ends up having to take a bit of a different approach on the deficit.
sentences.zh: 他赢得了相当令人信服的胜利，上台后最终不得不对赤字采取一种略有不同的方法。

sentences.en: Two years into his term, the deficit has reached what then seemed like an astounding figure of $200 billion.
sentences.zh: 在他任期的头两年里，赤字达到了在当时看来令人震惊的2000亿美元。

sentences.en: And Bush decides something must be done, and so he endorses a plan and eventually signs it that pairs some spending cuts with a tax increase in the name of deficit reduction.
sentences.zh: 布什认为必须采取行动，因此他支持并最终签署了一项计划，该计划以减赤的名义，将一些削减开支的措施与增税结合起来。

sentences.en: And he ends up paying a big price for this because he has broken a pledge he made to the American people.
sentences.zh: 结果他为此付出了沉重的代价，因为他违背了对美国人民的承诺。

sentences.en: Read my lips.
sentences.zh: 看我的嘴型。

sentences.en: Read his lips.
sentences.zh: 听他的嘴型。

sentences.en: No new taxes.
sentences.zh: 决不增税。

sentences.en: The price that he paid was that he loSt.
sentences.zh: 他付出的代价是他输了。

sentences.en: He lost re-election.
sentences.zh: 他输掉了连任竞选。

sentences.en: Now, it's not the only reason he lost to a surprisingly strong young upstart named Bill Clinton, but it is part of the reason,
sentences.zh: 现在，这并不是他输给一个实力惊人的年轻新秀比尔·克林顿的唯一原因，但这是原因之一，

sentences.en: is that many conservatives were demoralized with George H.W.
sentences.zh: 那就是许多保守派对乔治·H·W·布什加税感到士气低落。

sentences.en: Bush for raising taxes.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这最终对未来的共和党候选人和总统来说是一个非常重要的教训。

sentences.en: And this ends up being, I think, a very important lesson for future Republican candidates and presidents.
sentences.zh: 共和党人从乔治·H·W·布什应对赤字的经历中吸取了什么教训？

sentences.en: And what is the lesson that Republicans take from the George H.W.
sentences.zh: 布什。

sentences.en: Bush experience with deficits?
sentences.zh: 共和党人可以对比里根和乔治·H·W·布什的做法，并得出结论：如果你是一个共和党总统，赤字增加几乎没什么代价，相比之下增税则是必须要付出绝对代价的。

sentences.en: Republicans can look at the difference between Reagan and George H.W.
sentences.zh: 因此，乔治·H·W·布什失去了连任，部分原因是他优先考虑了降低债务和保持财政责任，事实证明人们其实并不那么在乎这些。

sentences.en: Bush and conclude that there is very little price to pay for deficit increases if you're a Republican president compared to tax increases, which you do absolutely pay a price for.
sentences.zh: 那么，下一个掌权的共和党总统会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: So George H.W.
sentences.zh: 在过去20年里，国家极大地繁荣了。

sentences.en: Bush loses his re-election in part because he prioritized lowering the debt, being fiscally responsible, which turns out people don't really care that much about.
sentences.zh: 然而具有讽刺意味的是，下一位上台的共和党总统乔治·W·布什并不太需要担心债务问题。

sentences.en: And so what happens to the next Republican president that comes into power?
sentences.zh: 但许多人感觉他们就像是在透过窗户看着别人的派对。

sentences.en: The country has prospered mightily over the past 20 years.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他面临着相反的问题。

sentences.en: Well, the irony is that the next Republican president who comes in, George W.
sentences.zh: 他继承了预算盈余，因为20世纪90年代末期的经济增长如此强劲，以至于政府的税收收入实际上超过了支出。

sentences.en: Bush, doesn't really have to worry about the debt.
sentences.zh: 所以在2000年的竞选活动中，这是一场激烈的争论。

sentences.en: But a lot of people feel as if they have been looking through the window at somebody else's party.
sentences.zh: 民主党人阿尔·戈尔希望把这笔钱存进社会保障的保险箱里。

sentences.en: In fact, he has the opposite problem.
sentences.zh: 但布什希望把它还给纳税人（正如他所说的那样），并进行大规模减税。

sentences.en: He's inherited a budget surplus because growth has been so strong at the end of the 1990s that the government's actually taking in more tax revenue than it is spending.
sentences.zh: 现在是把这些门窗统统敞开、邀请所有人进来的时候了。

sentences.en: So this was a big fight in the 2000 campaign.
sentences.zh: 是时候回报那些努力进入中产阶级的人们的劳动，并在他们需要的时候把更多的钱塞进他们口袋里了。

sentences.en: The Democrat, Al Gore, wanted to take that money and put it in a lockbox for Social Security.
sentences.zh: 我的减税计划做到了这一切，我希望你们能支持它。

sentences.en: But Bush wanted to give it back to taxpayers, as he called it, and do a big tax cut.
sentences.zh: 他削减了税收，然后经济陷入了一段时期的停滞。

sentences.en: It is time to fling those doors and windows open and invite everybody in.
sentences.zh: 出现了一次短暂的衰退。

sentences.en: It is time to reward the work of people trying to enter the middle class and put some more money in their pockets at a time when they need it.
sentences.zh: 9·11事件发生了。

sentences.en: My tax reduction plan does all these things, and I hope you'll support it.
sentences.zh: 他大幅增加了国家安全的开支。

sentences.en: He cuts taxes, and then the economy stalls out for a little bit.
sentences.zh: 最后，当布什总统在八年后卸任时，正值经济衰退之际，

sentences.en: There's a brief recession.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的是漫山遍野、飙升到没边的赤字。

sentences.en: 9-11 happens.
sentences.zh: 吉姆，在你讲述了这一切之后，

sentences.en: He ramps up spending on national security.
sentences.zh: 如果财政责任实际上并不是共和党总统执政的核心组成部分，为什么我们还要一直把共和党称作奉行财政责任的政党？

sentences.en: And then finally, when President Bush does leave office after eight years, at the time, in the midst of a recession,
sentences.zh: 我们之所以这么做，是因为共和党人在不在白宫时，在谈论赤字问题上声音极其响亮。

sentences.en: what we're seeing is skyrocketing deficits as far as the eye can see.
sentences.zh: 我们即将为这个法案中绝大多数并不需要的东西，花掉一万亿美元我们根本没有的钱。

sentences.en: Jim, after everything that you've just told us,
sentences.zh: 在过去的这几十年里，他们变得非常擅长利用赤字作为防御手段，来阻挠民主党总统可能采取的支出扩张。

sentences.en: why do we keep talking about Republicans as the party of fiscal responsibility if it's not actually a central component of how Republican presidents govern?
sentences.zh: 我今晚在这里告诉大家，我们崭新的多数派将准备采取不同的做法，采取一种华盛顿以前从未尝试过的新方法。

sentences.en: We do it because Republicans are so vocal in talking about deficits when they're not in the White House.
sentences.zh: 它从削减开支而不是增加开支开始。

sentences.en: We're about to spend a trillion dollars of money that we don't have for the vast majority of things in this bill that we don't need.
sentences.zh: 特别是在奥巴马执政时期。

sentences.en: And what they've gotten very good at doing over these last few decades is using deficits defensively against possible spending expansions by Democratic presidents.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，自从这位总统上台以来，已经累积了远超2万亿美元的额外债务。

sentences.en: I'm here to tell you tonight that our new majority will prepare to do things differently, to take a new approach that hasn't been tried in Washington before.
sentences.zh: 共和党人找到了一个非常有力的政治论点，他们说：

sentences.en: It starts with cutting spending instead of increasing it.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马医改给我们的赤字和国债增加了数万亿美元，并将这些债务负担推给了未来的几代人。

sentences.en: And in particular, in the Obama years.
sentences.zh: 支出过高，赤字过高，他们从总统执政的几乎一开始就利用这一论点来限制总统扩大支出的雄心。

sentences.en: We know that since this president has been in office, well over $2 trillion of additional debt has been amassed.
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，当共和党人谈论赤字和债务时，这实际上只是他们对那些他们不喜欢的支出说“不”的一种方式吗？

sentences.en: Republicans found a very strong political argument in saying,
sentences.zh: 是的，部分原因在于接下来发生的情况是，当他们在白宫掌权时，他们并没有付诸行动。

sentences.en: Obamacare adds trillions to our deficits and to our national debt and pushes those obligations on to coming generations.
sentences.zh: 那么，特朗普总统现在的做法，是否可以看作是你一直在描述的历史趋势的延续？共和党人已经吸取了教训，知道通过反对赤字和债务来进行竞选是有好处的，

sentences.en: Spending was too high, deficits were too high, and they used that argument to restrain the spending ambitions of the president almost from the very beginning of his presidency.
sentences.zh: 但一旦他们掌权，他们几乎立刻就会回避去完成真正解决赤字和债务所需的艰苦工作。

sentences.en: Is what you're saying that when Republicans talk about deficits and the debt, it's really a way of saying no to spending that they just don't like?
sentences.zh: 我认为特朗普总统是向里根和乔治·W·布什等历任共和党总统的财政政策的一种倒退，

sentences.en: Yes, in part because what then has happened is that when they get into power in the White House, they don't follow through.
sentences.zh: 即共和党人一旦掌控白宫，就愿意借钱来减税，也愿意借钱来资助更多的军事开支。

sentences.en: So can what President Trump is doing be seen as just a continuation of this historical trend that you've been describing where Republicans have learned that it's good to campaign against the deficit and the debt.
sentences.zh: 他们愿意为自己喜欢的项目增加赤字。

sentences.en: But once they get into power, they almost immediately shy away from doing the hard work required to actually solve the deficit and the debt.
sentences.zh: 但现在，无论是这两位总统中的哪一位，还是奥巴马总统，与特朗普总统在处理赤字问题上的做法之间，存在着一个巨大的区别。

sentences.en: I see President Trump as a reversion to the fiscal policies of past Republican presidents such as Reagan and George W.
sentences.zh: 而这个区别在于，在每一位前总统的情况下，当时都发生了经济衰退。

sentences.en: Bush, where Republicans are, once they have the White House, willing to borrow money to cut taxes and willing to borrow money to fund more military spending.
sentences.zh: 而在特朗普总统的情况下，他面对的是一个可以说是极其火热的经济，一个自大衰退以来以数年未见的速度增长的经济。

sentences.en: They're willing to increase deficits for the programs they like.
sentences.zh: 共和党人找到了一个非常有力的政治论点，他们说：

sentences.en: But there's a big difference right now between either of those presidents or President Obama and what President Trump is doing with deficits.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马医改给我们的赤字和国债增加了数万亿美元，并将这些债务负担推给了未来的几代人。

sentences.en: And that difference is in each of those presidents' cases, there was a recession.
sentences.zh: 支出过高，赤字过高，他们从总统执政的几乎一开始就利用这一论点来限制总统扩大支出的雄心。

sentences.en: And in President Trump's case, he's got a red hot, so to speak, economy, an economy that is growing faster than it has in several years since the Great Recession.
sentences.zh: 你的意思是，当共和党人谈论赤字和债务时，这实际上只是他们对那些他们不喜欢的支出说“不”的一种方式吗？

sentences.en: So if President Trump isn't under economic pressure to increase the debts, if there isn't a financial reason to do it or a war that requires lots of spending,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果特朗普总统在增加债务方面没有面临经济压力，如果没有财政上的原因或者需要大量开支的战争，

sentences.en: that would explain it, why is he running up the debt so much?
sentences.zh: 这就说得通了，那他为什么还要积累这么多债务呢？

sentences.en: If you look at what it actually would take to bring down the debt or even just bring down the deficit, balance the budget,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看要削减债务甚至仅仅是削减赤字、平衡预算究竟需要付出什么，

sentences.en: that means tax hikes or big spending cuts for programs people like.
sentences.zh: 那就意味着加税，或者对人们喜爱的项目进行大幅削减开支。

sentences.en: There's just no incentive to do that.
sentences.zh: 根本就没有这样做的动力。

sentences.en: And when you have a president like Trump who has campaigned almost entirely on not having tradeoffs, on being able to do everything,
sentences.zh: 当你遇到像特朗普这样的总统时，他的竞选几乎完全建立在没有权衡、能够做到一切的承诺之上，

sentences.en: then it gets very, very hard to imagine a scenario in which deficit reduction becomes a real priority of the White House and therefore of Congress because it's hard.
sentences.zh: 那么就很难、非常难想象出这样一种情景：赤字削减成为白宫乃至国会的真正首要任务，因为这太难了。

sentences.en: And people don't like the choices that result from it a lot of the time.
sentences.zh: 而且人们往往不喜欢由此带来的选择。

sentences.en: Don't you remember when Republicans howled to high heaven that President Obama was spending us into the gutter, spending us into oblivion?
sentences.zh: 你不记得当年的情形吗？当时共和党人对奥巴马总统把美国的花销搞得一团糟、把美国花进无底深渊发出了震天的抗议。

sentences.en: And now Republicans are doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 而现在，共和党人却在做同样的事情。

sentences.en: And Jim, what about the rest of the Republican Party?
sentences.zh: 吉姆，那共和党其他成员呢？

sentences.en: What are they doing now that Republican President Donald Trump is increasing the national debt?
sentences.zh: 共和党籍总统唐纳德·特朗普正在增加国债，他们现在在做什么？

sentences.en: A few of them are howling like Rand Paul of Kentucky.
sentences.zh: 极少数人在抗议，比如来自肯塔基州的兰德·保罗。

sentences.en: If you were against President Obama's deficits and now you're for the Republican deficits, isn't that the very definition of hypocrisy?
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经反对奥巴马总统的赤字，而现在又支持共和党的赤字，这不正是虚伪的定义吗？

sentences.en: But most of them are just kind of being quiet about it.
sentences.zh: 但他们大多数人对此都只是保持沉默。

sentences.en: Madam President, I'm pleased to announce that our bipartisan, bicameral negotiations on defense spending and other priorities have yielded a significant agreement.
sentences.zh: 参议院议长女士，我很高兴地宣布，我们在国防开支和其他优先事项上的两党、两院谈判已经达成了一项重要协议。

sentences.en: We're doing this one.
sentences.zh: 我们正在推进这一项。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Because we don't want to see the surprise for the military.
sentences.zh: 因为我们不想看到军方遭遇突发状况。

sentences.en: We have an opioids crisis in America.
sentences.zh: 我们美国正面临阿片类药物危机。

sentences.en: Let's get on with fixing it.
sentences.zh: 让我们着手解决它吧。

sentences.en: We think we can get pretty darn close on cancer research and getting some cures.
sentences.zh: 我们认为我们在癌症研究和寻找某些治愈方法方面可以非常接近目标。

sentences.en: So let's let's keep that going.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们继续保持下去。

sentences.en: If a Martian came to Earth in the year 2018 and heard some of these speeches from Senate Republicans,
sentences.zh: 如果有一个火星人在2018年来到地球，并听到参议院共和党人的这些发言，

sentences.en: that Martian would have a hard time realizing that the Republicans traditionally were the party of the balanced budget.
sentences.zh: 那个火星人很难意识到传统上共和党是主张平衡预算的党派。

sentences.en: Jim, at the start of our conversation, we talked about this enduring reputation that the Republican Party has for fiscal responsibility, for budget restraint.
sentences.zh: 吉姆，在对话开始时，我们谈到了共和党一直以来在财政责任和预算克制方面的声誉。

sentences.en: Does that still exist?
sentences.zh: 这种声誉现在还存在吗？

sentences.en: Republicans have a self-professed reputation as the party that cares about fiscal restraint.
sentences.zh: 共和党人自诩为关心财政克制的党派。

sentences.en: But if they still believe that deficits are bad and spending is bad, they are not acting like it right now in Washington.
sentences.zh: 但如果他们仍然认为赤字不好、花钱不好，他们现在在华盛顿的表现可一点也不像那么回事。

sentences.en: And it sounds from everything we've just discussed that they haven't really acted that way for decades.
sentences.zh: 从我们刚才讨论的一切来看，他们似乎几十年来一直都不是这样的。

sentences.en: With the exception of President George H.W.
sentences.zh: 除老布什总统外，

sentences.en: Bush, Republican presidents have not made a serious effort to keep the budget deficit in check for a really long time.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，共和党总统并没有为控制预算赤字做出严肃的努力。

sentences.en: This may sound like a very simple, maybe even stupid question, but why does it matter if a country like the United States has a lot of debt?
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能是一个非常简单、甚至有点愚蠢的问题，但为什么像美国这样的国家背负大量债务会有关系呢？

sentences.en: What's the inherent problem or is there an inherent problem with running a deficit and having debt?
sentences.zh: 其内在的问题是什么，或者说出现赤字和债务本身有什么问题吗？

sentences.en: There are two big reasons.
sentences.zh: 有两个重大原因。

sentences.en: One is political.
sentences.zh: 一个是政治上的。

sentences.en: Americans, in general, want government to act more or less a bit like themselves or their business.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，美国人希望政府的行为或多或少能像他们自己或他们的企业那样。

sentences.en: That's how people expect government to work.
sentences.zh: 人们就是这样期望政府运作的。

sentences.en: They want it to live within its means.
sentences.zh: 他们希望政府量入为出。

sentences.en: And when we get too far out of whack of that, there tend to be political consequences.
sentences.zh: 当我们的做法与此严重脱节时，往往会产生政治后果。

sentences.en: The other reason why people worry about deficits, politicians do, is a concern that high debt eventually will hold back economic growth.
sentences.zh: 人们和政治家担心赤字的另一个原因，是担心高额债务最终会阻碍经济增长。

sentences.en: And it can do that in a couple of ways.
sentences.zh: 它可以通过几种方式做到这一点。

sentences.en: It can crowd out private investment because money that would be going to private businesses is instead being lent to the government.
sentences.zh: 它会挤出私人投资，因为原本要流向私营企业的资金转而被借给了政府。

sentences.en: Or over time, if the debt piles up too high, creditors begin to worry about your ability to repay.
sentences.zh: 或者随着时间的推移，如果债务累积得太高，债权人就会开始担心你的偿还能力。

sentences.en: And in that case, they charge you higher costs to borrow money from them.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，他们会向你收取更高的借贷成本。

sentences.en: And then it gets into a cycle.
sentences.zh: 然后这就进入了一个循环。

sentences.en: And then you're in for a rude jolt when you have to someday just raise taxes a bunch or cut spending a bunch or both just to keep the lights on in the government.
sentences.zh: 接着，当你有一天不得不大幅增税、大幅削减开支，或者双管齐下仅仅为了维持政府运转时，你就会迎来当头一棒。

sentences.en: So in the meantime, Republicans can use the deficit as a potent political tool, it sounds like you're saying,
sentences.zh: 听起来你的意思是，在此期间，共和党人可以把赤字当作一个强有力的政治工具，

sentences.en: without really being concerned about the economic consequences of the deficit.
sentences.zh: 而完全不必担心赤字带来的经济后果。

sentences.en: We are not seeing any real indication right now that markets or anybody sees the United States as about to default or in a big economic risk zone due to the amount of money that it's borrowing.
sentences.zh: 我们目前没有看到任何真正的迹象表明，市场或任何人认为美国由于借款数额巨大而即将违约或处于巨大的经济风险区。

sentences.en: The question is, how close are we to that?
sentences.zh: 问题是，我们距离那个地步还有多近？

sentences.en: I would argue we're not that close to the danger point as Republicans were telling us that we were.
sentences.zh: 我认为，我们并没有像共和党人告诉我们的那样，离危险点那么近。

sentences.en: Now, that could change.
sentences.zh: 当然，这可能会改变。

sentences.en: But at this point, those economic reasons aren't the things being debated.
sentences.zh: 但在目前，引发辩论的并非这些经济原因。

sentences.en: It's political reasons.
sentences.zh: 而是政治原因。

sentences.en: Thank you, Jim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，吉姆。

sentences.en: Really appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日新闻简报 DealBook 的商业和政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的一些领袖，包括万斯、

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、吉尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的实时对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download The New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限来阅读我们的所有新闻。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你绝对不想错过。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, in testimony before the Senate, the director of national intelligence, Dan Coats, warned that Russia is likely to try to meddle in this fall's congressional elections.
sentences.zh: 周二，国家情报总监丹·科茨在参议院作证时警告称，俄罗斯可能会试图干预今秋的国会选举。

sentences.en: Frankly, the United States is under attack.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，美国正受到攻击。

sentences.en: Under attack by entities that are using cyber to penetrate virtually every major action that takes place in the United States.
sentences.zh: 遭到那些利用网络渗透美国几乎所有重大活动的实体的攻击。

sentences.en: As with Russia's interference in the presidential race,
sentences.zh: 正如俄罗斯干预总统竞选一样，

sentences.en: Coats said that the Kremlin's goal in this year's elections would be to create political confusion and undermine America's democratic values.
sentences.zh: 科茨表示，克里姆林宫今年选举的目标是制造政治混乱并破坏美国的民主价值观。

sentences.en: There should be no doubt that Russia perceived that its past efforts as successful and views the 2018 U.S.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，俄罗斯认为其过去的努力是成功的，并将2018年美国

sentences.en: midterm elections as a potential target for Russian influence operations.
sentences.zh: 中期选举视为俄罗斯施加影响行动的潜在目标。

sentences.en: And after a year-long investigation into corruption, police in Israel have recommended that the country's prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, be charged with bribery, fraud,
sentences.zh: 在进行了长达一年的腐败调查后，以色列警方建议对该国总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡提出受贿、欺诈指控，

sentences.en: and breach of truSt.
sentences.zh: 以及背信罪。

sentences.en: Netanyahu is accused of accepting hundreds of thousands of dollars in gifts from political allies, including jewelry, cigars, and champagne,
sentences.zh: 内塔尼亚胡被指控接受了政治盟友价值数十万美元的礼物，包括珠宝、雪茄和香槟，

sentences.en: and of striking a secret deal to ensure positive coverage from one of Israel's largest newspapers, charges he denies.
sentences.zh: 并达成了一项秘密协议，以确保以色列最大的一家报纸对其实施正面报道，但他否认了这些指控。

sentences.en: I feel a great responsibility to continue to lead Israel in a way that will secure its future.
sentences.zh: 我感到责任重大，要继续以保障以色列未来发展的方式领导以色列。

sentences.en: In a speech to Israelis on Tuesday night, Netanyahu made clear he would not resign.
sentences.zh: 内塔尼亚胡周二晚间在向以色列人发表的讲话中明确表示他不会辞职。

sentences.en: That the only thing that interests me is the good of the country, not for cigars, not for press coverage, not for anything.
sentences.zh: 唯一让我感兴趣的是国家利益，不是雪茄，不是媒体报道，什么都不是。

sentences.en: Only the good of the country.
sentences.zh: 只有国家利益。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是今天的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》将为假期接待客人做好准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，了解如何让你的客人宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是那种一觉睡到天黑的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝断片去睡觉。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有对什么过敏或饮食禁忌吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们爱喝咖啡还是茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 请在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢收听播客的任何地方查找《Wirecutter秀》。
